content: Approximately 8.03% of the superoxide present in the cytosol of a typical cell exists in its protonated form. This proportion is supported by the scientific literature, as evidenced by a PubMed search. At the time of analysis, only 28 articles included terms such as HO2, hydroperoxyl, or perhydroxyl in their titles, compared to 9,228 articles mentioning superoxide. It is argued here that this disparity in attention is not justified. The biological and biomedical significance of HO2 far surpasses the level of attention it has received in research. Several key observations from recent years are reviewed, and these findings can be more effectively explained by considering the involvement of HO2-. It is proposed that a broader recognition of the potential role of HO2in biological systems would greatly benefit biomedical research. The dielectric constant has a significant influence on pKa, and because the dielectric constant of air is very low, superoxide generated photochemically in the atmosphere is almost entirely present as HO2. HO2 is highly reactive and functions as a cleanser of the atmosphere by breaking down certain organic pollutants. Consequently, the chemistry of HO2 holds substantial geochemical importance.
